chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq, from one whom he mentioned, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in al-sammur, al-sinjab, and foxes, and he said: “There is no good in all of that except al-sinjab, for it is an animal that does not eat meat.”

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبِ: foxes, whose fur is included among what is disapproved for prayer
key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sammur, a type of fur or animal hide mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.السِّنْجَابِ: sinjab, the squirrel whose fur is excepted in the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.اللَّحْمَ: meat, mentioned as the basis for distinguishing the animal
key_terms.دَابَّةٌ: a creature or animal, describing the nature of al-sinjab

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat wearing squirrel fur or fox fur according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the permissibility of performing salat (prayer) in garments made from certain animal furs. It states that prayer in these materials is not acceptable except for al-sinjab, because it is an animal that does not eat meat.
